sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: No macro signal in the tracked set is flagged extreme heading into the week; the two strongest reads are both equity-side and pointing the same way — Nasdaq 100 sits +1.94 z above its 3-year mean and the S&P 500 is close behind at +1.91 z, both reflecting a market that has re-rated sharply higher rather than any stress event. Treasuries lean the other way: the 20y+ ETF sits at -1.64 z (long yields elevated vs. the 3-year window), while gold's +1.53 z keeps a mild safety bid alive alongside the equity rally. The S&P 500 gained roughly 4.1% over the trailing month, climbing from 7,428.78 to 7,730.99 and sitting near the top of its 1-month range (7,316-7,799). VIX at 14.55 (-0.59 z) shows no volatility premium building into next week's reports.

sections.heading: What to watch

Thu: LULU US (consumer-cyclical, -0.51% median across 423 names) and CPRT US (industrials) round out the week.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Mining leads the reaction table into the week at +6.62% median across 151 tickers with a thick 2,626-item news window; copper follows at +2.63% median but on just 6 names and 247 news items — a real but thin signal. Oil-gas sits at the other extreme, -2.15% median across 33 names on a comparably thick 1,007-item news count, making it the one sector-level read this week backed by both direction and volume in a bearish sense.
